messages.text: Based on current vault evidence, what are the strongest opportunities for Signaling / Non-signaling Tester in Semiconductor, and what evidence supports each opportunity?

I queried the current RS knowledge vault. Based on the Raw evidence returned, the strongest Semiconductor opportunities for Signaling / Non-signaling Testers are:

| Rank | Opportunity | Why it is strong | Supporting Raw evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Non-signaling production / ATE / multi-port production test** using **CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100** | This is the clearest “semiconductor production” opportunity: the evidence explicitly frames the customer need as **non-signaling ATE or multi-port production test**, and positions R&S instruments as the answer. | “Do you need non-signaling ATE or multi-port production test? ✔ If yes → CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 = Only R&S.” — `raw/Productions/2026_02_CMX500_Amarisoft_Sales_Battle_Card.md`, section 5 |
| 2 | **Modem-RF / chipset validation for FR1 + FR3 and 6G readiness** using **CMX500 + RFU18** | Strong semiconductor fit because the DUT is a **Qualcomm Mobile Test Platform powered by Qualcomm Modem-RF System**, and the stated validation targets are **RF performance and protocol behavior** across FR1/FR3 aggregation. | “CMX500… extended with the new RFU18 board to provide coverage up to 18 GHz… path to extend existing testers towards 6G… Qualcomm… Mobile Test Platform powered by the Qualcomm® Modem-RF System, enabling comprehensive validation of RF performance and protocol behavior across the aggregated FR1 and FR3 bands.” — `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz demonstrates FR1–FR3 carrier aggregation, advancing 6G readiness.md`, section 4 |
| 3 | **5G NR / NR-NTN / RedCap / Wi‑Fi 7 signaling validation platform** using **CMX500** | Strong because it shows CMX500 as a future-proof callbox spanning cellular and non-cellular technologies in one instrument. This maps well to semiconductor modem/connectivity roadmap validation, especially where chipsets must support multiple standards. | “The CMX500 radio communication tester supports cellular technologies such as LTE, 5G NR, as well as non-cellular technologies like Wi‑Fi, all in a single instrument. The latest test feature sets, including… NR‑NTN, 5G RedCap, and Wi‑Fi 7, provides a long-term, future-proof callbox platform.” — `raw/Productions/PR/SPEAG combines CMX500 OBT with the DASY8-3D system for automated SAR testing of 5G NR devices.md`, section 3 |
| 4 | **OTA performance validation for Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G RedCap devices** using **CMX500 + OTA chambers** | This is slightly less directly semiconductor-specific than production ATE or Qualcomm modem validation, but the evidence is strong for device performance validation workflows that semiconductor customers often need for reference designs, modules, and end-device enablement. | “EMITE’s… over-the-air chambers can now be combined with… R&S CMX500… supporting… LTE, 5G NR FR1… FR2… including… 5G RedCap… supports… Wi‑Fi 7… customers obtain a comprehensive environment for accurately assessing the performance of Wi‑Fi 7 as well as 5G Red Cap devices.” — `raw/Productions/PR/EMITE and Rohde & Schwarz join forces to support OTA measurements on Wi-Fi 7 and 5G RedCap.md`, section 3 |
| 5 | **Advanced 5G protocol/signaling validation: Release 19 MIMO, MAC/PDSCH, codeword behavior** | Opportunity is supported by evidence of unresolved signaling questions around MAC/PDSCH and high-layer MIMO behavior. This is more “R&D / protocol conformance / modem stack validation” than production. | “What does the signaling from MAC look like? Additional info in one PDSCH allocation or two PDSCH allocation, how to know if two CW are used? Cross-check if there are FPGA reference sizes for TBS_LBRM.” — `raw/Knowledge/Release 19 MIMO With DL greater 4 PDSCH layers (6x6, 8x8).md`, section 146 |

**Bottom line:**  
The strongest vault-backed opportunity is **non-signaling semiconductor production test / ATE / multi-port production test** with **CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100**. The strongest signaling-side opportunity is **CMX500-based modem-RF validation**, especially **FR1–FR3 aggregation, RF/protocol behavior validation, and 6G-readiness** with semiconductor players such as Qualcomm explicitly present in the evidence.

Next, you could ask for this to be turned into a sales playbook by customer type: **chipset vendor, module maker, device OEM, test lab, or OSAT/production line**.

answer.text:
**FR3 / 5G NR R&D signaling test opportunity** — strongest because the RAW evidence explicitly names a “multi-technology, multi-channel one-box signaling tester” and says its versatility supports adaptation to different NR numerologies, making it “the ideal choice for FR3 research and development” [8].
**5G NR MAC/PDSCH signaling and modem validation opportunity** — supported by evidence of unresolved signaling/test questions around MAC signaling, PDSCH allocation structure, whether two codewords are used, and FPGA reference sizes for TBS_LBRM, indicating a need for tester support in protocol/signaling validation workflows [2].
**NTN, shared-spectrum, and UE capability signaling test opportunity** — supported by evidence that UE capabilities must indicate NTN SSB-based RRM measurements, support for multiple SMTCs, and propagation-delay compensation for NTN and shared spectrum channel access [5].
**SUL / random-access carrier-selection signaling test opportunity** — supported by evidence that UEs select NR UL or SUL for random access based on SIB1 and RACH configuration signaling, including the configured RSRP threshold for SUL selection [6].
**Beam-management and multi-cell reporting test opportunity** — supported by evidence that beam selection is performed across configured cells, M × L beams are reported in a single report instance, and maximum M/L values depend on UE capability and reporting configuration [7].

cited_passages.text: EMITE’s state-of-the-art over-the-air chambers can now be combined with the latest sophisticated testing features of the [R&S CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") one-box signaling tester from Rohde & Schwarz. The radio communication tester offers a wide range of device testing capabilities, supporting cellular technologies such as LTE, 5G NR FR1 frequency range up to 8 GHz and FR2 millimeter wave frequency range up to 50 GHz, including the latest 5G RedCap technology. It also supports non-cellular technologies, including the latest Wi-Fi 7, all in a single instrument. As a consequence of this collaboration, EMITE’s customers obtain a comprehensive environment for accurately assessing the performance of Wi-Fi 7 as well as 5G Red Cap devices.

cited_passages.text: At the heart of the test setup is the [CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") one-box signaling tester from Rohde & Schwarz, extended with the new RFU18 board to provide coverage up to 18 GHz. RFU18 is a modular hardware upgrade for the CMX500 platform, giving customers a straightforward, cost-effective path to extend existing testers towards [6G](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/solutions/wireless-communications-testing/wireless-standards/6g/6g-overview_253278.html "6G"). As device under test (DUT), Qualcomm Technologies provided a Mobile Test Platform (MTP) powered by the Qualcomm® Modem-RF System, enabling comprehensive validation of RF performance and protocol behavior across the aggregated FR1 and FR3 bands.
